readme.html:
Surehand MCP lets the AI app you already use work inside Adobe® After Effects®, and shows you what it did. It is for motion designers, finishing artists and technical directors who can't deliver on "the AI says it's done". Every edit is one undo step and comes back with an exact list of what changed. Structural changes come with pixel proof that the picture didn't change. Deliveries are checked against your own spec, templates are pushed through worst-case inputs, and every version built from data is checked row by row. Verified, not trusted.

  • AI apps: Claude (Desktop and Code), ChatGPT (desktop app and web), Codex, Cursor, VS Code (GitHub Copilot), Windsurf / Devin Desktop, LM Studio, or any MCP client. Inside After Effects, the Surehand panel can also chat through Codex, Claude Code or Antigravity on your own sign-in.
  • After Effects: 2025 and 2026 on macOS and Windows, in any language, are tested release by release. The extension loads in CC 2019 (16.0) and newer; versions before 2025 are best effort.
  • Install: signed and notarized .pkg for Mac, signed Setup.exe for Windows. No administrator rights, no account. Free and open source (MIT).
  • Website and downloads: conformlabs.co/surehand.

It doesn't generate images and ships no presets or canned looks. It works on your project, by your rules, and measures the result.

AI app ──MCP──> surehand-ae server (Node, on your computer) ──localhost──> Surehand panel (CEP, inside After Effects) ──> ExtendScript

See it work

Four short demos, recorded on Surehand 1.4.1 and After Effects 2026. Long waits are cut and marked on screen; nothing is sped up. All four as a playlist, or on conformlabs.co/surehand.

  • Precomp surgery: Claude un-precomposes a comp, keeps every expression working and proves the picture didn't change (16 frames, zero difference).
  • Preflight: a comp checked against the client's delivery spec finds 5 problems, each with a timecode, then one is fixed and checked again.
  • Stress test: a lower-third template with long German names, Arabic, Hebrew and huge numbers; 28 of 33 variants break, and the original comp is confirmed unchanged.
  • Farm render: a render split across 4 aerender processes, and every one of the 250 frames verified.

What you can ask it

Real requests, in your words. The AI picks the tool; the tool does the measuring.

You ask The tool
"Check Endcard against our broadcast spec before I send it." ae_preflight: the comp and the rendered file against your delivery spec, with timecoded findings
"Stress-test the lower third with long German names and Arabic." ae_stress_test: worst-case inputs through every control, each result measured, your comp left untouched
"Un-precompose Logo_Lockup and prove nothing changed." ae_precomp_surgery: rehearsed on a scratch copy, applied only when the pixels match
"Why does this render slowly? Speed it up only where the picture stays identical." ae_render_profile: a timeline cost map, then speed-ups kept only when proven identical
"Split the render across 3 processes and prove every frame is there." ae_farm: chunks, aerender scripts, a local parallel run and a completeness check
"Make a version of Score Card for every row of scores.csv, and check each one before you queue them." ae_versions_from_data: one undo step, every row read back and measured
"Export the texts for the Hebrew and French translators. When they come back, fit them: tracking down to -40, never below 36 px." ae_localize: CSV or XLIFF out, a checked version per language back in
"Make a 9:16 of Promo. Logo pinned 80 px from the top, titles inside title-safe." ae_reformat: your rules, checked on every frame
"I inherited this project. What does the render queue actually pull in, and what's fragile?" ae_project_xray: a read-only explanation, with precise locations
"What changed between v11 and v12?" ae_project_history: snapshots and a readable diff

Everyday edits work the same way: comps, layers, keyframes at Graph Editor precision, expressions, effects, text, masks, 3D, audio, footage, Essential Graphics and render settings, plus any After Effects script when no tool fits. See the full tool list.

Install

Download the latest release

Your setup Download
Mac Surehand-MCP-<version>.pkg (signed and notarized)
Windows Surehand-MCP-Setup-<version>.exe (signed)
Claude Desktop only Surehand-MCP.mcpb
Setups the installers don't cover Surehand-MCP-<version>.zip (Mac and Windows scripts; open START HERE.txt)

Nothing else is needed: the .pkg and Setup.exe include Node.js 24, the .mcpb uses Claude Desktop's built-in Node.js, and the zip's installer downloads Node.js if it is missing.

Step-by-step setup guides for each AI app: Claude, ChatGPT and Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, LM Studio.

Mac and Windows installers

  1. Mac: double-click Surehand-MCP-<version>.pkg and follow the steps. No administrator password: everything goes into your own home folder. Windows: run Surehand-MCP-Setup-<version>.exe. It installs per user, with no administrator rights.
  2. Restart After Effects once.
  3. Restart the AI apps that were open during the install.

Both installers put a private Node.js 24, the server and the After Effects extension on your computer, connect the AI apps they find, and write the Surehand skills for them (see The installer).

First run

The bridge starts with After Effects; nothing needs to be opened. To see it, open Window > Extensions > Surehand MCP. A green dot means connected. The panel shows the latest calls, the permission mode and Pause AI.

Then ask your AI app something simple:

"Check After Effects is connected, then make a 1080p comp with an animated title and show me frame 1."

If something is off, the panel's ☰ › Test the connection (or surehand-ae selftest) says what and how to fix it.

Claude Desktop only (.mcpb)

Double-click Surehand-MCP.mcpb and click Install in Claude Desktop, then restart After Effects once. On first start the server installs its After Effects extension by itself. Use either the .mcpb or an installer for Claude Desktop, not both.

The zip

The same installer as double-click scripts, for setups the installers don't cover:

Surehand-MCP/
  START HERE.txt
  1. Claude Desktop (easiest)/   Surehand-MCP.mcpb
  2. Mac/                        1. Install, 2. Test Installation, 3. Connect ChatGPT, 4. Uninstall (.command)
  3. Windows/                    1. Install, 2. Test Installation, 3. Connect ChatGPT, 4. Uninstall (.bat)
  Support files/                 run.sh, run.ps1, surehand-ae.mjs, this README

Double-click 1. Install in 2. Mac or 3. Windows, then restart After Effects once. With After Effects open, 2. Test Installation checks everything. START HERE.txt (from installer/START HERE.txt) has the same steps in plain language, including what to do if macOS Gatekeeper or Windows SmartScreen blocks the files.

The installer

What every installer (.pkg, Setup.exe, or 1. Install from the zip) does:

  • uses the private Node.js 24 that the .pkg / Setup.exe put in ~/.surehand/node; the zip's scripts use the Node.js on your PATH, or download a private Node.js 22 LTS into ~/.surehand/node (checksum-verified)
  • copies the MCP server to ~/.surehand/ae/server/surehand-ae.mjs (one self-contained file)
  • installs the After Effects extension into your user CEP extensions folder. The extension is signed, so it loads without enabling unsigned extensions (PlayerDebugMode)
  • creates ~/.surehand/ae/config.json with a random access token
  • registers the server, under the name surehand-ae, with the AI apps it finds: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT desktop / Codex (~/.codex/config.toml, created if the ChatGPT or Codex app is installed), Cursor, VS Code (its user mcp.json, used by GitHub Copilot's Agent mode), Windsurf / Devin Desktop (~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json, %APPDATA%\devin on Windows, and Windsurf's ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json while that folder is there) and LM Studio (~/.lmstudio/mcp.json). Before a config file is changed, a timestamped backup is made next to it (*.surehand-<time>.bak, the newest three are kept); the very first original also stays as *.surehand.bak. If Claude Desktop is open it offers to restart it, because a running Claude Desktop overwrites its config file
  • writes the Surehand skills (see Skills) for the AI apps that read skill files, and the zips to upload in Claude Desktop chat

The server also checks the After Effects extension every time it starts and installs or updates it if needed.

To uninstall: double-click 4. Uninstall from the zip, or run surehand-ae uninstall (and remove the .mcpb in Claude Desktop > Settings > Extensions if you used it). Checkpoints are kept unless you pass --all.

Skills

Four Agent Skills teach the AI how to work with Surehand well:

  • surehand-ae: the basics. Check the connection, read before editing, confirm each edit with its change report, look at the result, never work around a refusal, plus the ExtendScript traps seen live.
  • surehand-ae-delivery: preflight against your own delivery spec, stress tests, versions from data checked row by row, the localization round trip, farm renders.
  • surehand-ae-safe-restructure: structural edits and render speed-ups with pixel proof.
  • surehand-ae-timing-layout: exact keyframes, easing, measured alignment and reformats.

The source is skills/ in this repo.

  • The installer writes them to ~/.claude/skills/ (Claude Code; Cursor and VS Code read it too) and ~/.agents/skills/ (ChatGPT desktop / Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf / Devin Desktop); %USERPROFILE% on Windows. A folder is written only when one of those apps is on the computer (or the folder is there already). Only the four surehand-ae* folders are written, replaced on update and removed on uninstall; other skills are never touched.
  • For Claude Desktop chat: upload the skills in Customize › Skills › Upload a skill (files in ~/.surehand/ae/skills, one zip per skill). claude.ai takes the same zips.
  • surehand-ae skills [--json] shows where they are installed; surehand-ae skills install / uninstall writes or removes them.

Claude Code plugin

In Claude Code you can also install Surehand as a plugin (the server and the four skills, from the latest release; needs Node.js on your PATH):

/plugin install surehand-ae --marketplace ConformLabs/surehand-mcp

The server installs the After Effects extension the first time it starts; restart After Effects afterwards.

Other MCP clients

Point them at the installed server (stdio):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "surehand-ae": { "command": "/path/to/node", "args": ["/Users/<you>/.surehand/ae/server/surehand-ae.mjs"] }
  }
}

The panel's ☰ › Connect an AI app shows which apps are connected and connects the others.

For AI agents that install MCP servers themselves (Cline, for example), llms-install.md has the steps: download, checksum, install, MCP settings.

ChatGPT

ChatGPT desktop app (Mac and Windows): no tunnel needed. It runs local MCP servers itself and reads the same ~/.codex/config.toml as Codex, which the installer fills in. Restart ChatGPT after installing; surehand-ae appears under Settings > Plugins > Servers (switch it on). To add it by hand: Add > MCP server > STDIO, command = the Node path printed by the installer, argument = ~/.surehand/ae/server/surehand-ae.mjs.

ChatGPT on the web (chatgpt.com) can only reach MCP servers over public HTTPS, so the server runs in HTTP mode behind a temporary tunnel. The panel's ☰ › ChatGPT on the web screen runs it in the background (and can download Cloudflare's cloudflared for you); see the wiki page. By hand:

  1. Install a tunnel tool once: cloudflared (no account needed: brew install cloudflared on macOS, winget install --id Cloudflare.cloudflared on Windows) or ngrok.
  2. Double-click 3. Connect ChatGPT in the zip's 2. Mac or 3. Windows folder (or run surehand-ae chatgpt). It prints a URL like https://xxxx.trycloudflare.com/mcp/<token>.
  3. In ChatGPT: Settings > Apps & Connectors > Advanced settings > Developer mode on, then Create a connector, paste the URL, choose No authentication (the token is in the URL), and save.
  4. In a chat, enable the connector from the tools menu. Keep the tunnel running while you use it.

The URL contains your secret token: anyone with it can run scripts on your machine while the tunnel is up. Quick-tunnel URLs change on every start, so update the connector URL each time (or set up a named Cloudflare tunnel). To rotate the token, delete token from ~/.surehand/ae/config.json and re-run the installer, then restart After Effects.

Safety model

Surehand is built so that you stay in charge of the project, and so that what the AI says it did can be checked.

Permissions, Pause AI and undo

Permissions. The mode selector Full / Ask / Read-only at the top of the Surehand panel (or "permissions" in ~/.surehand/ae/config.json) applies to the next request, with no restart:

Mode What happens
Full (default) Everything runs. Your AI app may still ask you before each tool call.
Ask Every edit and script waits in the Surehand panel, showing the exact code or arguments, until you click Allow or Deny. When the panel is closed, an approval pop-up appears instead. Reads are not held.
Read-only Tools that edit are refused. Scripts still run (to read information), but if one changes the project it is undone immediately and the AI is told what it tried to change. Scripts that touch the undo history (executeCommand, beginUndoGroup, endUndoGroup, purge) or do things that can't be undone (opening, closing or saving projects, newProject, quit, rendering, scheduleTask, saving preferences) are refused before they run. This is a text check (comments are ignored, escapes are decoded; a name inside a string or on another object counts too): a call assembled at runtime gets past it, and is then undone at most once, checked with a temporary undo marker, and reported if the project isn't back.

Pause AI. One click in the panel, and every AI call is refused until you resume.

Undo. Every tool call is one undo step, and ae_undo reverts it and reports what was reverted. ae_batch runs many steps as one undo step, all or nothing by default. The panel's activity feed has Undo on the most recent change, offered only when nothing has changed the project since. After Effects itself can split a few operations into several undo steps (seen with comp duplicates, layer copies and source replacements); where that can happen, the result names the exact way back instead (a checkpoint, or a command that removes exactly the copies it made). See Limits.

Checkpoints. ae_checkpoint saves a timestamped copy of the project, and restores one as a new file next to the original; the original is never overwritten. Tools that make big changes (precomp surgery, render optimizations, versions, reformats) can save one first. The panel lists them under ☰ › Checkpoints.

Existing files are never replaced silently. Save As, frame and contact-sheet output paths, frame exports, handoff packages, farm plans and farm renders refuse when a file is already there; the AI passes overwrite: true only when replacing it is intended.

Shell commands in scripts (system.callSystem) can be switched off separately (☰ › Shell commands in scripts).

What the AI can and can't do

  • It can do anything an After Effects script can: ae_run_script runs JavaScript in After Effects (modern syntax is converted for ExtendScript), and the ready-made tools cover the common work with checks built in.
  • It can't approve its own requests, get past Pause AI, or press the panel's buttons. Approvals, Pause AI and the panel's own actions need a secret that the bridge keeps in memory and hands only to the Surehand panel and the approval pop-up through After Effects' extension events, never over the network or in a file. A new request can't be answered in its first second on screen, and Enter never allows.
  • It sees what it asks to see: tool results, and frames it renders. Your project files stay on your computer; what your AI app sends to its provider (your messages, tool results, rendered frames) follows that provider's terms.
  • Permissions are guardrails against mistakes, not a sandbox. A script can still read and write files. An AI app with full shell access as your user account can read and change everything Surehand can, including config.json.

Activity log. Every tool call is recorded in ~/.surehand/ae/activity.jsonl with time, AI app, tool, arguments (including the full script code), duration and result. The panel shows the latest calls, ☰ › Activity history lists them (click one for what changed), Open log file there reveals the file, and surehand-ae activity prints it.

Security

  • The bridge listens on 127.0.0.1 only and requires the token from ~/.surehand/ae/config.json (file mode 600); requests from web pages (with an Origin header) are rejected.
  • ae_run_script can do anything an After Effects script can, including reading and writing files and running shell commands via system.callSystem. Only connect AI apps you trust, and keep the ChatGPT tunnel running only while you use it.
  • What the token protects against: other users of the computer, and programs that can't read your files. What it doesn't: a program running as your own user account with access to your files.
  • Chat in After Effects never stores or handles an API key or sign-in: the AI agent runs on its own sign-in.
  • Settings files of AI apps are only changed when they can be read (a file with a mistake in it is left as it is and reported), with a timestamped backup first (the newest three are kept) and an atomic write.
  • surehand-ae diagnostics and Copy diagnostics in the panel contain no secrets.

Self-test

surehand-ae selftest (or 2. Test Installation, or the panel's Test the connection) checks every link of the chain: the config and token, the extension and its signature, the AI apps' settings, the bridge inside After Effects, ExtendScript, the scripting preference, a small non-destructive test job (a temporary comp with text, keyframes and an effect) and a frame preview. A failed check says how to fix it.

surehand-ae selftest --full runs every major tool (over 60 steps) against temporary comps (removed afterwards; if the open project has no unsaved changes, the Save As and checkpoint-restore checks briefly switch to a scratch project and then reopen it), lists which scripting features your After Effects version has, and saves a report to ~/.surehand/ae/compat/. All steps pass on After Effects 2025 (25.6) and 2026 (26.5) on macOS and on 2026 on Windows 11, also with 2025 and 2026 running side by side; the panel, permissions, approvals and background rendering are verified on macOS and Windows. Please share reports from other versions.

What it does, by job

Check and deliver

Preflight (ae_preflight) checks the comp, and optionally the rendered file, against your delivery spec: a small JSON file with the numbers from your client's or broadcaster's document. Nothing is built in. It covers comp settings, missing items, text inside safe areas on every frame, cap height and reading speed, and in the file: codec, levels, loudness, black and frozen frames and a flash pre-check. A check that couldn't run makes the verdict INCOMPLETE, never PASS. The stress test (ae_stress_test) pushes worst-case inputs (long German and Finnish strings, Hebrew and Arabic, CJK, emoji, huge and negative numbers) through every control a template exposes and measures each result on a scratch copy; it also lists expressions that break in other After Effects languages. ae_project_health lists missing footage, fonts and effects, expression errors and unused items. Details: Preflight, Preflight: rendered files, Stress test.

Restructure safely

Every edit returns a change report computed by After Effects itself. ae_prove_identical renders reference frames, lets the edit happen and renders them again: identical, identical within tolerance, or differs with a difference image. ae_precomp_surgery un-precomposes or deep-duplicates with every expression reference rewritten, rehearses the change on a scratch copy and applies it only when the pixels match; what it can't reproduce exactly is refused with the reason. ae_replace_in_expressions does project-wide find and replace with a dry run. Details: Change report, Proven edits, Precomp surgery.

Timing and layout

The keyframe table (ae_get_keyframes, ae_set_keyframe_table) reads and writes keys in frames or seconds with the exact speed and influence After Effects stores. ae_copy_ease copies an ease to other keys, ae_audit_easing checks motion against the project's own most-used curves, and ae_retime_keyframes scales, offsets, staggers or conforms by whole frames. ae_align_layers aligns and distributes by measured on-screen bounds, not anchor points, and reports any residual. ae_get_layer_bounds, ae_sample_pixels, ae_render_frame and ae_render_contact_sheet let the AI measure and look at the result.

Versions, localization and reformats

ae_versions_from_data turns a CSV or JSON file into versions of a template comp in one undo step, then reads every row back where it renders: text, number format, colour rules, overflow, safe areas, bar sizes against your mapping. ae_localize exports texts with their context to CSV or XLIFF and brings translations back as a version per language, fitted only by the adjustments you allow, with right-to-left handled. ae_reformat makes 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 or any size from your rules (cover, safe areas, pins, scale limits) and checks the result on every frame. When a rule can't be met, the report says FAIL and why; it doesn't decide for you. Details: Versions from data, Localization, Reformat.

Renders and farms

ae_render_profile shows where render time goes across the whole timeline, then applies chosen speed-ups one at a time and keeps only those proven identical, with the time saved. ae_handoff_package collects a project for someone else with a manifest of what they need (fonts, plug-ins, colour settings) and can prove the package renders the same. ae_farm lists what a render needs on a node and checks a node against it, splits a render into chunks for local processes or other machines, runs them here in parallel, and proves the chunks add up. ae_render_background runs aerender in a separate process while After Effects stays usable. Details: Render profile, Handoff package, Render farm.

Understand a project

ae_project_xray explains an inherited project without changing it: what the render queue renders, what every expression depends on and which links are fragile, what is missing, footage specs and what makes it heavy. ae_project_history snapshots the project and diffs any two versions or checkpoints into a readable change list. ae_get_comp_map maps nested precomps, parenting, mattes and expression links. Details: Project X-ray, Project history.

Chat in After Effects

☰ › Chat with your AI app in the Surehand panel runs Codex, Claude Code or Antigravity, on your own sign-in and subscription, with Surehand's tools as its only tools. The same mode, approvals, Pause AI and activity log apply. In AI apps that show interactive views (for example Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, VS Code and Cursor), Preflight, X-ray, the stress test, proofs and history diffs come with an in-chat view: findings on a timeline, frames, before and after. Other apps get the same results as text. Details: Chat with your AI app, In-chat views.

Reference

All tools

Surehand has up to 114 ready-made tools, plus ae_run_script for anything else.

Run anything:

Tool
ae_run_script Run JavaScript in After Effects; return a value to get it back as JSON. Modern syntax (let/const, arrows, template strings, destructuring, classes, ?., ??, for...of) and common built-ins (map, filter, Object.keys, JSON...) work: the code is converted for AE's ES3 engine with Babel, keeping line numbers. Errors come back with the failing line, the code around it, and a hint. log() output is returned. One undo step per call.
ae_run_script_file Run a .jsx / .jsxbin file from disk with arguments.
ae_get_scripting_guide ExtendScript cheat sheet for the model (also an MCP resource aemcp://docs/extendscript).

By area:

  • Workflow: ae_batch (many tool steps or scripts in one call and ONE undo step, with one change report; atomic by default: if a step fails everything is undone), ae_checkpoint (save a timestamped copy of the project, list, restore as a new file next to the original; the original is never overwritten; each checkpoint also gets a history snapshot), ae_list_scripts (your scripts: AE's Scripts folder, ScriptUI Panels, and folders listed as "scriptFolders" in ~/.surehand/ae/config.json, with their descriptions) + ae_run_script_file, ae_tools and ae_call (every tool on demand, see Tool profiles)
  • Verification: ae_prove_identical (Proven edits), ae_precomp_surgery (Precomp surgery), ae_project_history (Project history)
  • Checks and delivery: ae_preflight (Preflight), ae_stress_test (Stress test), ae_project_health (missing footage/fonts/effects, expression errors, unused footage, empty comps/folders, duplicate comp names)
  • Versions: ae_versions_from_data (Versions from data), ae_localize (Localization), ae_reformat (Reformat)
  • Understanding: ae_project_xray (Project X-ray), ae_get_comp_map (nested precomps, parenting, track mattes, expression references)
  • Seeing the result: ae_render_frame (a frame as an image; options: zoom into a region, render only some layers, transparency on a checkerboard or a color, difference image against another time or comp), ae_render_contact_sheet (a grid of frames across time, labelled with time and frame number, to judge motion and easing). The temporary comp stays until After Effects has written the image, then it is removed and anything switched for the render set back by hand, and the project is compared with how it was. They never use Edit > Undo (it could revert your own last step); After Effects may list a "Surehand MCP preview" step, which only brings the preview's own changes back. In a 32 bpc project, or one with "Blend Colors Using 1.0 Gamma", frames are rendered at 16 bpc without it, so colors look as in the viewer (After Effects writes such frames far too dark); the project settings are put back. ae_export_frames does the same. ae_prove_identical always renders with the project's own settings, so a capture and its comparison match.
  • Measuring: ae_get_layer_bounds (exact on-screen boxes after transforms, parenting, 3D and camera; in-frame and action/title-safe checks), ae_sample_pixels (rendered RGBA/hex at points)
  • Status & app: ae_status, ae_system_info, ae_execute_menu_command, ae_undo, ae_redo, ae_purge, ae_get_fonts, ae_reload_helpers
  • Project: ae_get_project_info, ae_list_items, ae_get_item_info, ae_import_files, ae_create_folder, ae_move_items, ae_rename_item, ae_remove_items, ae_replace_footage, ae_save_project, ae_open_project, ae_new_project
  • Compositions: ae_list_comps, ae_get_comp_info, ae_create_comp, ae_set_comp_settings, ae_duplicate_comp, ae_open_comp, ae_precompose, ae_add_comp_marker
  • Layers: ae_get_layer_info, ae_add_layer (solid, text, shape, null, adjustment, camera, light, footage/comp), ae_set_layer_attributes (switches, timing, parent, blend mode, track matte, order...), ae_delete_layers, ae_duplicate_layer, ae_split_layer, ae_get_selection, ae_select_layers, ae_set_text
  • Properties & animation: ae_get_properties, ae_find_properties (search all layers by name/match name, or list animated / expression properties), ae_set_property, ae_set_keyframes (interpolation + easing), ae_remove_keyframes, ae_set_expression, ae_get_expressions
  • Expressions: ae_check_expression (try an expression and see errors and values without keeping it), ae_replace_in_expressions (project-wide find & replace, dry run, errors after the change)
  • Keyframes (Graph Editor level): ae_edit_keyframes (value, move in time, in/out interpolation, speed + influence per dimension, continuous/auto-Bezier, spatial tangents, roving, keyframe color labels, delete), ae_copy_keyframes (between properties/layers/comps, time range, offset), ae_set_time_remap (keys or freeze frame). The keyframe tools take whole frames (frame, moveToFrame, frames, offsetFrames) as well as seconds.
  • Precision timing and easing: ae_get_keyframes (a keyframe table across many layers and properties: whole frame and exact time of every key, exact value, interpolation, speed + influence per dimension exactly as After Effects stores them, tangents, roving; keys between frames are flagged; optional normalised curve numbers per segment), ae_set_keyframe_table (write such a table back, many properties in one undo step, every attribute exact), ae_copy_ease (the exact ease of a reference key onto keys of other properties and layers, with a stated rule for different dimension counts), ae_audit_easing (motion consistency against the project's own most-used curves: lists the segments that match none), ae_retime_keyframes (scale around an anchor, offset or stagger by whole frames, conform to a new frame rate; keeps the curves' shape, refuses keys colliding on a frame)
  • Measured layout: ae_align_layers (align, distribute and centre by real on-screen bounds, through parenting, scale, rotation and text glyph boxes, not anchor points; reports any residual after the move)
  • Effects, shapes & masks: ae_list_available_effects, ae_get_effect_params (an effect's exact parameter names, types, defaults and ranges, without touching your layers), ae_apply_effect, ae_set_effect_params, ae_remove_effect, ae_apply_preset (an animation preset .ffx file by path), ae_add_shape, ae_add_mask
  • Text: ae_style_text_range (per-character styling by range or matching words), ae_set_paragraph (justification, indents, spacing, box size), ae_add_text_animator (animator properties + range/wiggly/expression selector)
  • 3D: ae_set_camera (one/two-node, focal length in mm, depth of field; reports angle of view), ae_set_light (type, color, intensity, cone, falloff, shadows), ae_set_material (material options, lists the 3D renderers)
  • Audio: ae_audio_to_keyframes (Convert Audio to Keyframes), ae_audio_markers (markers at beats/peaks)
  • Color: ae_color_settings (Adobe or OCIO color engine, working space, bit depth, linearization, OCIO spaces)
  • Footage:

skills.name: surehand-ae-delivery
skills.description: Checks After Effects comps and renders against the user's delivery spec, stress-tests them, builds checked versions, readies farm renders. Use for QC, stress tests, versions, localization, farms.

skills.name: surehand-ae-safe-restructure
skills.description: Restructures After Effects projects without changing the picture (un-precompose, merge precomps, bake expressions, reorder effects) with pixel proof. Use for cleaning up an inherited .aep.

skills.name: surehand-ae-timing-layout
skills.description: Sets exact After Effects keyframe timing and easing, aligns layers by measured bounds and reformats comps by the user's rules. Use for keyframes, easing, retiming, layout or reformats.

skills.name: surehand-ae
skills.description: Works in Adobe After Effects (AE) through Surehand MCP. Reads the project first, edits comps, layers, keyframes and expressions, verifies every change. Use for any AE or .aep task.
